one: AI 的“总览课”：把搜索、MDP、概率图模型、逻辑和机器学习放进同一个“有限信息 + 有限算力下做决策”的框架里。
title: Artificial Intelligence: Principles and Techniques
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has had a huge impact in many areas, including medical diagnosis, speech recognition, robotics, web search, advertising, and scheduling. This course focuses on the foundational concepts that drive these applications. In short, AI is the mathematics of making good decisions given incomplete information (hence the need for probability) and limited computation (hence the need for algorithms). Specific topics include search, constraint satisfaction, game playing,n Markov decision processes, graphical models, machine learning, and logic. Prerequisites: CS 103 or CS 103B/X, CS 106B or CS 106X, CS 109, and CS 161 (algorithms, probability, and object-oriented programming in Python). We highly recommend comfort with these concepts before taking the course, as we will be building on them with little review.
prereq: CS 103（或 103B/X）、CS 106B（或 106X）、CS 109、CS 161；官方明确要求“不要指望课上补这些基础”。
topics: **搜索与约束满足**：DFS/BFS/A*、启发式、CSP、局部搜索
**博弈与对抗搜索**：minimax、alpha-beta、期望效用
**MDP 与强化学习**：值迭代、策略迭代、Q-learning 基础
**概率图模型**：贝叶斯网络、HMM、变量消元、采样
**机器学习**：朴素贝叶斯、感知机、逻辑回归、损失函数与正则化
**逻辑与知识表示**：命题逻辑、一阶逻辑、推理
**综合项目**：把上述模块组合成一个可运行的 AI 系统
assessment: 通常为 5 次左右书面/编程作业 + 期中 + 期末 + 一个综合项目；工作量在 Stanford 课程里偏大。具体比例以当季官网为准。
who: 想建立完整 AI 知识地图的本科生/转专业学生；之后准备读 CS 229/224N/234 的人；以及想补“经典 AI”这一块的工程师。
tips: 先补概率（CS 109）和算法（CS 161），否则作业会很痛苦。作业里的搜索和 MDP 部分建议自己从零写一遍，不要只调库。

zh: 自然语言处理与深度学习
one: NLP 从 word2vec 到 LLM 的核心课：作业实现 word2vec、RNN、注意力，最后做一个 LLM 项目。
title: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning (LINGUIST 284, SYMSYS 195N)
description: Methods for processing human language information and the underlying computational properties of natural languages. Focus on deep learning approaches: understanding, implementing, training, debugging, visualizing, and extending neural network models for a variety of language understanding tasks. Exploration of natural language tasks ranging from simple word level and syntactic processing to coreference, question answering, and machine translation. Examination of representative papers and systems and completion of a final project applying a complex neural network model to a large-scale NLP problem. Prerequisites: calculus and linear algebra; CS124, CS221, or CS229.
prereq: 微积分与线性代数；CS 124、CS 221 或 CS 229 之一。
topics: **词表示**：word2vec、GloVe、子词/tokenization
**语言模型**：n-gram、RNN/LSTM、注意力
**Transformer**：self-attention、位置编码、架构细节
**预训练模型**：BERT、GPT、T5、缩放规律
**适配与对齐**：微调、提示、RLHF、DPO
**NLP 任务**：句法、语义、问答、机器翻译、信息抽取
**final project**：通常是 LLM/agent 相关的研究或应用
assessment: 通常为 4–5 次作业 + 期中 + final project；作业包含大量 PyTorch 实现。具体以当季官网为准。
who: NLP/LLM 方向必选；想做 agent、RAG、对齐、多模态语言模型的人；想从传统 NLP 转向 LLM 的工程师。
tips: 先修 CS 229 或至少理解 softmax/交叉熵/反向传播。想深入“从零训练 LLM”，接着上 CS 336。

one: 图机器学习：GNN、知识图谱、影响力最大化，把关系数据变成可学习的表示。
title: Machine Learning with Graphs
description: Many complex data can be represented as a graph of relationships between objects. Such networks are a fundamental tool for modeling complex social, technological, and biological systems. This course focuses on the computational, algorithmic, and modeling challenges specific to the analysis of massive graphs. By means of studying the underlying graph structure and its features, students are introduced to machine learning techniques and data mining tools apt to reveal insights on a variety of networks. Topics include: representation learning and Graph Neural Networks; algorithms for the World Wide Web; reasoning over Knowledge Graphs; influence maximization; disease outbreak detection, social network analysis. Prerequisites: CS109, any introductory course in Machine Learning.
prereq: CS 109；一门入门机器学习课程。
topics: **图基础**：中心性、社区发现、幂律、图生成
**节点嵌入**：DeepWalk、node2vec、矩阵分解
**GNN**：GCN、GraphSAGE、GAT、消息传递
**知识图谱**：TransE、RotatE、查询与推理
**传播与影响力**：独立级联、线性阈值、影响力最大化
**图生成与自监督**：图对比学习、扩散
**项目**：通常用真实图数据做预测/分析
assessment: 作业 + 项目；编程以 PyTorch/PyG 为主。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 社交网络、推荐、风控、生物网络、知识图谱方向；想补“非欧几里得数据”建模的人。
tips: 先理解消息传递范式，再学各种 GNN 变体。项目可以结合 CS 246 的大规模数据方法。

one: 概率图模型的系统课：表示、推断、学习三件套，是理解贝叶斯方法和结构化预测的基础。
title: Probabilistic Graphical Models: Principles and Techniques
description: Probabilistic graphical modeling languages for representing complex domains, algorithms for reasoning using these representations, and learning these representations from data. Topics include: Bayesian and Markov networks, extensions to temporal modeling such as hidden Markov models and dynamic Bayesian networks, exact and approximate probabilistic inference algorithms, and methods for learning models from data. Also included are sample applications to various domains including speech recognition, biological modeling and discovery, medical diagnosis, message encoding, vision, and robot motion planning. Prerequisites: basic probability theory and algorithm design and analysis.
prereq: 基础概率论；算法设计与分析。
topics: **表示**：贝叶斯网络、马尔可夫网络、因子图
**精确推断**：变量消元、信念传播、junction tree
**近似推断**：变分推断、MCMC、重要性采样
**参数学习**：MLE、EM、隐变量模型
**结构学习**：评分搜索、约束方法
**时序模型**：HMM、动态贝叶斯网络
**应用**：语音、生物、医疗诊断、视觉、机器人规划
assessment: 作业 + 期中 + 项目；偏数学与实现结合。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 想做概率建模、因果、贝叶斯深度学习的人；NLP/计算生物/机器人中需要处理不确定性的研究者。
tips: 和 CS 229 互补：229 偏预测，228 偏“结构化不确定性”。变量消元和 VI 建议手推一遍。
note: 2026-27 学年未在 ExploreCourses 排课。

one: Stanford ML 旗舰课：用概率和统计把监督学习、无监督学习和学习理论串成一套完整框架。
title: Machine Learning (STATS 229)
description: Topics: statistical pattern recognition, linear and non-linear regression, non-parametric methods, exponential family, GLMs, support vector machines, kernel methods, deep learning, model/feature selection, learning theory, ML advice, clustering, density estimation, EM, dimensionality reduction, ICA, PCA, reinforcement learning and adaptive control, Markov decision processes, approximate dynamic programming, and policy search. Prerequisites: knowledge of basic computer science principles and skills at a level sufficient to write a reasonably non-trivial computer program in Python/NumPy to the equivalency of CS106A, CS106B, or CS106X, familiarity with probability theory to the equivalency of CS 109, MATH151, or STATS 116, and familiarity with multivariable calculus and linear algebra to the equivalency of MATH51 or CS205.
prereq: 能写 Python/NumPy 程序（CS 106A/B 级）；概率（CS 109/MATH 151/STATS 116）；多变量微积分与线性代数（MATH 51/CS 205）。
topics: **监督学习**：线性/逻辑回归、广义线性模型、SVM、核方法、树模型与集成
**学习理论**：偏差-方差、正则化、特征选择、泛化与模型选择
**无监督学习**：k-means、GMM、EM、PCA、ICA、密度估计
**深度学习基础**：神经网络、反向传播、训练技巧
**强化学习**：MDP、值迭代、策略搜索、自适应控制
**课程项目**：通常是一个开放式的 ML 研究/应用项目
assessment: 通常为 4–5 次 problem sets + 期中 + final project；每周约 10–15 小时。具体比例以当季官网为准。
who: 想真正理解 ML 数学原理、之后做研究或读博的人；已经会用 sklearn 但想补推导和理论的工程师；准备面试但不想只背题的人。
tips: problem set 的推导一定要自己写一遍，尤其是 GLM、SVM 对偶和 EM。配合 CS 229M 或 STATS 315A 可以补齐理论侧。

one: 机器学习理论：泛化界、非凸优化、隐式正则，回答“为什么深度学习能工作”。
title: Machine Learning Theory (STATS 214)
description: How do we use mathematical thinking to design better machine learning methods? This course focuses on developing mathematical tools for answering this question. This course will cover fundamental concepts and principled algorithms in machine learning, particularly those that are related to modern large-scale non-linear models. The topics include concentration inequalities, generalization bounds via uniform convergence, non-convex optimization, implicit regularization effect in deep learning, and unsupervised learning and domain adaptations. Prerequisites: MATH 51 and STATS 117 and either CS 229 or STATS 315A. See https://statistics.stanford.edu/course-equiv for equivalent courses in other departments that satisfy these prerequisites.
prereq: MATH 51；STATS 117；CS 229 或 STATS 315A。
topics: **集中不等式**：Hoeffding、Chernoff、McDiarmid
**泛化理论**：一致收敛、VC 维、Rademacher 复杂度
**非凸优化**：梯度下降、鞍点、landscape
**隐式正则**：过参数化、双下降、边缘稳定
**无监督与域适应**：表示学习理论
**现代模型分析**：Transformer/深度网络的近似与泛化
assessment: 作业 + 期末/项目，以证明和论文阅读为主。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 想做 ML theory、读博、或需要严谨分析能力的研究者；也适合数学/统计背景转 ML 的人。
tips: 先补实分析和概率论。不要指望一次听懂，配合讲义和论文反复推。
note: 2026-27 学年未在 ExploreCourses 排课。

one: Ng 的深度学习实战课：从全连接到 CNN/RNN，重点是“把 DL 项目做成功”，而不只是推公式。
title: Deep Learning
description: Deep Learning is one of the most highly sought after skills in AI. We will help you become good at Deep Learning. In this course, you will learn the foundations of Deep Learning, understand how to build neural networks, and learn how to lead successful machine learning projects. You will learn about Convolutional networks, RNNs, LSTM, Adam, Dropout, BatchNorm, Xavier/He initialization, and more. You will work on case studies from healthcare, autonomous driving, sign language reading, music generation, and natural language processing. You will master not only the theory, but also see how it is applied in industry. You will practice all these ideas in Python and in TensorFlow, which we will teach. AI is transforming multiple industries. After this course, you will likely find creative ways to apply it to your work. This class is taught in the flipped-classroom format. You will watch videos and complete in-depth programming assignments and online quizzes at home, then come in to class for advanced discussions and work on projects. This class will culminate in an open-ended final project, which the teaching team will help you on. Prerequisites: Familiarity with programming in Python and Linear Algebra (matrix / vector multiplications). CS 229 may be taken concurrently.
prereq: Python 编程；线性代数（矩阵/向量运算）；CS 229 可以同时修。
topics: **神经网络基础**：前向/反向传播、激活函数、损失函数
**CNN**：卷积、池化、经典架构、迁移学习
**序列模型**：RNN、LSTM、注意力机制
**训练技巧**：Adam、Dropout、BatchNorm、Xavier/He 初始化
**ML 项目方法论**：误差分析、偏差-方差、数据划分、迭代策略
**行业案例**：医疗影像、自动驾驶、音乐生成、NLP
**开放式 final project**
assessment: 编程作业 + 在线 quiz + 开放式 final project；翻转课堂要求课前投入。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 想快速上手深度学习工程、做完整项目的人；产品/创业背景但需要技术落地能力的人；比 CS 231N 更偏“广度 + 项目”的路线。
tips: 如果完全没接触过 DL，先看 CS 229 的 NN 部分或 CS 231N 前几讲。项目比作业更能拉开差距，建议早组队、早定题。

zh: 计算机视觉的深度学习
one: CV 领域最有名的深度学习课：从 kNN 到 Transformer，作业是自己手写反向传播并训练 CNN。
title: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
description: Computer Vision has become ubiquitous in our society, with applications in search, image understanding, apps, mapping, medicine, drones, and self-driving cars. Core to many of these applications are visual recognition tasks such as image classification and object detection. Recent developments in neural network approaches have greatly advanced the performance of these state-of-the-art visual recognition systems. This course is a deep dive into details of neural-network based deep learning methods for computer vision. During this course, students will learn to implement, train and debug their own neural networks and gain a detailed understanding of cutting-edge research in computer vision. We will cover learning algorithms, neural network architectures, and practical engineering tricks for training and fine-tuning networks for visual recognition tasks.Prerequisites: Proficiency in Python - All class assignments will be in Python (and use numpy) (we provide a tutorial here for those who aren't as familiar with Python). If you have a lot of programming experience but in a different language (e.g. C/C++/Matlab/Javascript) you will probably be fine.College Calculus, Linear Algebra (e.g. MATH 19, MATH 51) -You should be comfortable taking derivatives and understanding matrix vector operations and notation. Basic Probability and Statistics (e.g. CS 109 or other stats course) -You should know basics of probabilities, gaussian distributions, mean, standard deviation, etc.
prereq: 熟练 Python/NumPy；微积分与线性代数（MATH 19/51）；概率统计基础（CS 109 级）。
topics: **图像分类**：kNN、线性分类器、损失函数与优化
**神经网络**：反向传播、多层网络、激活函数
**CNN 架构**：AlexNet、VGG、ResNet、高效网络
**训练工程**：初始化、归一化、正则化、学习率、数据增强
**可视化与可解释性**：显著图、特征可视化、对抗样本
**检测/分割**：R-CNN 系列、YOLO、语义/实例分割
**前沿**：视频、生成模型、多模态、Transformer
**final project**：通常做真实视觉任务
assessment: 3 个编程作业 + final project；作业量较大但非常值。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 想做 CV、多模态、机器人感知、自动驾驶的人；想补“深度学习底层实现”能力的工程师；准备读视觉方向博士的人。
tips: A2 的 BatchNorm 和 A3 的 Transformer 建议手写，不要抄。final project 不要只刷 SOTA，做一个能讲清楚 error analysis 的小问题更加分。

one: 强化学习核心课：MDP、值迭代、策略梯度、探索，作业包含 deep RL。
title: Reinforcement Learning
description: To realize the dreams and impact of AI requires autonomous systems that learn to make good decisions. Reinforcement learning is one powerful paradigm for doing so, and it is relevant to an enormous range of tasks, including robotics, game playing, consumer modeling and healthcare. This class will briefly cover background on Markov decision processes and reinforcement learning, before focusing on some of the central problems, including scaling up to large domains and the exploration challenge. One key tool for tackling complex RL domains is deep learning and this class will include at least one homework on deep reinforcement learning. Prerequisites: proficiency in python, CS 229 or equivalents or permission of the instructor; linear algebra, basic probability.
prereq: 熟练 Python；CS 229 或同等 ML 基础；线性代数与概率。
topics: **MDP 基础**：回报、贝尔曼方程、策略评估
**动态规划**：值迭代、策略迭代
**无模型方法**：蒙特卡洛、TD、Q-learning、SARSA
**函数逼近**：线性逼近、深度 Q 网络
**策略梯度**：REINFORCE、actor-critic、PPO
**探索**：ε-greedy、UCB、 Thompson sampling
**深度 RL 与离线 RL**：实践中的稳定性问题
**项目**：通常训练一个 agent 解决控制/游戏任务
assessment: 通常为 3–4 次作业 + 期中 + 项目；至少一次 deep RL 作业。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 机器人、RL 研究、游戏 AI、推荐系统方向；想做具身智能的人。
tips: 先把 MDP 和动态规划吃透，再上深度 RL。作业里的 exploration 部分建议配合 Sutton & Barto 第 2–3 章。
note: 2026-27 学年未在 ExploreCourses 排课，以最近一次开设的资料整理。

one: 深度生成模型的理论课：VAE、GAN、flow、diffusion 的概率基础与训练算法。
title: Deep Generative Models
description: Generative models are widely used in many subfields of AI and Machine Learning. Recent advances in parameterizing these models using neural networks, combined with progress in stochastic optimization methods, have enabled scalable modeling of complex, high-dimensional data including images, text, and speech. In this course, we will study the probabilistic foundations and learning algorithms for deep generative models, including Variational Autoencoders (VAE), Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), and flow models. The course will also discuss application areas that have benefitted from deep generative models, including computer vision, speech and natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Prerequisites: Basic knowledge about machine learning from at least one of CS 221, 228, 229 or 230. Students will work with computational and mathematical models and should have a basic knowledge of probabilities and calculus. Proficiency in some programming language, preferably Python, required.
prereq: CS 221/228/229/230 至少一门；概率与微积分；Python 编程。
topics: **概率基础**：极大似然、变分推断、ELBO、MCMC
**VAE**：重参数化、后验坍塌、层次化 VAE
**GAN**：对抗训练、模式崩溃、Wasserstein GAN
**Flow 模型**：可逆变换、Jacobian、连续流
**Energy-based 模型**：对比散度、score matching
**Diffusion**：DDPM、score-based、classifier-free guidance
**应用**：图像、文本、语音、RL
**项目**：生成模型的研究或应用
assessment: 作业 + 期中/期末 + 项目；数学推导和实现并重。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 想做扩散模型、图像/视频生成、生成式 AI 研究的人；想理解 VAE/GAN 背后概率原理的人。
tips: 先补变分推断和 score matching，否则 diffusion 部分会很吃力。配合 CS 236G 可以补 GAN 的工程细节。

one: 机制可解释性：probing、steering、causal abstraction、sparse autoencoders，理解模型内部到底在算什么。
title: Mechanistic Interpretability
description: What is the internal structure of modern neural networks and how can we study it? This course provides a broad and deep introduction to interpretability, the subfield of machine learning concerned with understanding precisely how models process information and why they produce the outputs they do. We will cover topics such as probing, steering, causal abstraction, and sparse autoencoders, with a particular emphasis on causal methods and large language models. The course will include guest lectures from leading interpretability labs across academia and industry.
prereq: 深度学习/LLM 基础；概率与线性代数；最好读过 Transformer。
topics: **Probing**：线性探针、表征分析、局限性
**Steering**：激活干预、方向向量、因果追踪
**Causal abstraction**：因果图、干预、抽象映射
**Sparse autoencoders**：字典学习、特征分解、单义性
**Circuits**：注意力头、MLP 神经元、组合结构
**LLM 内部机制**：事实回忆、推理、欺骗
**可解释性与安全**：如何用于审计和 alignment
assessment: 作业 + 项目/论文复现；偏研究与讨论。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 想做 interpretability、AI safety、模型审计的人；想理解 LLM 内部机制的研究者。
tips: 先读 Anthropic 的“Towards Monosemanticity”和“Scaling Monosemanticity”，以及 causal abstraction 相关论文。

one: 用 agent-based model 和 generative agents 模拟人类社会，做“what if”实验。
title: AI Agents and Simulations (PSYCH 186)
description: How might we craft simulations of human societies that reflect our lives? Many of the greatest challenges of our time, from encouraging healthy public discourse to designing pandemic responses, and building global cooperation for sustainability, must reckon with the complex nature of our world. The power to simulate hypothetical worlds in which we can ask "what if" counterfactual questions, and paint concrete pictures of how a multiverse of different possibilities might unfold, promises an opportunity to navigate this complexity. This course presents a tour of multiple decades of effort in social, behavioral, and computational sciences to simulate individuals and their societies, starting from foundational literature in agent-based modeling to generative agents that leverage the power of the most advanced generative AI to create high-fidelity simulations. Along the way, students will learn about the opportunities, challenges, and ethical considerations in the field of human behavioral simulations. Prerequisites: Team projects and some course assignments will involve programming in Python. Having a background in human-centered design (e.g., CS 147, ME 115A, or a class from the d.school), AI (e.g., CS 221, CS 224), or social psychology may be helpful, although it is not required.
prereq: Python 编程；AI（CS 221/224）、人本设计或社会心理学背景有帮助，但不强制。
topics: **Agent-based modeling**：规则、涌现、校准
**社会模拟**：意见传播、合作、公共政策
**Generative agents**：LLM 驱动的人格、记忆、规划
**反事实实验**：what-if 场景设计
**评估**：模拟保真度、偏差、可复现性
**伦理**：操纵、隐私、模拟的权力
**团队项目**：构建一个社会模拟
assessment: 团队项目为主 + 课程作业/讨论。具体以当季官网为准。
who: 计算社会科学、多 agent 系统、AI 政策/伦理方向；想做社会模拟或生成式 agent 的人。
tips: 先读 Generative Agents（Park et al., 2023）和经典 Schelling/NetLogo 模型。项目要注意可复现性和伦理边界。

one: 把 LLM 变成能查、能推理、能执行长任务的 agent：RAG、工具、知识库、形式化方法、长程规划。
title: Agentic AI
description: AI agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) are already transforming how we work, learn, and solve problems - and we are only at the beginning. As these systems grow more capable, they hold extraordinary promise for accelerating scientific discovery and democratizing access to high-quality medical, legal, and educational services worldwide. This is a project course coupled with rigorous lectures on the principles, methodologies, and cutting-edge research underlying agentic AI. Students undertake a substantial quarter-long project in either foundational methodology research or building novel agents in a domain of their choice. Topics covered include: (1) minimizing hallucination in question-answering and task-oriented agents using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and formal task descriptions; (2) hybrid knowledge reasoning over databases, knowledge bases, and unstructured text; (3) AI-driven knowledge curation and discovery for scientific research; (4) improving the accuracy and interpretability of decision-making agents through formal methods; and (5) automated techniques for improving the accuracy and efficiency of long-horizon agents. title: Self Improving AI Agents
description: This graduate seminar course covers the latest techniques and applications of AI agents that can continuously improve themselves through interaction with themselves and the environment. The course will start with self-improvement techniques for LLMs, such as constitutional AI, using learned/domain-specific verifiers, scaling test-time compute, and combining search with LLMs. We will then discuss the latest research in augmenting LLMs with tool use and retrieval techniques, and orchestrating AI capabilities with multimodal web interaction. We will next discuss multi-step reasoning and planning problems for agentic workflows, and the challenges in building robust evaluation and orchestration frameworks. Industry applications that will be discussed include coding agents, research assistants in STEM, robotics and more. Students will work on an original research project in this area, discuss the suggested readings in each class, and learn from invited academic and industry speakers. description: Machine learning from human preferences (MLHP) provides mechanisms for optimizing systems that are used by humans - with applications in personalization, finetuning, and assistance. MLHP has been important to successes in modern language modeling, but the technical and conceptual underpinnings are spread across fields: psychometrics, discrete choice, reinforcement learning, information retrieval, and normative theory. This course will provide a careful and practical introduction to the main methods and models of MLHP. It will cover: choice modeling and its axiomatic approaches; imitation and static and active learning of choice; reinforcement learning from human feedback; assistance games, bandits, and recommendation; behavioral biases, style control; aggregation and fairness. This is a graduate-level course. By the end of the course, students should be able to build, analyze, and optimize systems that are used by humans.

title: Artificial General Intelligence for Reasoning, Planning, and Decision Making
description: Course Description:Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized AI through remarkable pattern matching capabilities. However, the path to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) requires advancing beyond unconscious (System 1) to conscious (System 2) processing. This research-oriented course explores fundamental approaches to elevate LLMs toward AGI capabilities through conscious reasoning, planning, and decision-making. Core Research Questions: 1. How can we enable LLMs to transition from pattern matching to conscious deliberation? 2. What frameworks support robust reasoning and verifiable decisions? 3. How do we implement planning and temporal awareness in LLM systems? 4. What role does multi-LLM agent collaboration play in advancing toward AGI capabilities? The course examines: 1. Theoretical foundations of consciousness in AI 2. Multi-LLM Agent Collaborative Intelligence (MACI) frameworks 3. Entropy-guided information exchange 4. Constitutional AI principles 5. Temporal reasoning and planning architectures. Through lectures, discussions, and hands-on projects, students will explore practical implementations across various domains. While healthcare provides immediate applications (diagnosis, treatment planning), the principles apply broadly to any field requiring AGI-level reasoning capabilities. description: The course is concerned with the design and operation of the network fabrics which interconnect large-scale compute and storage nodes in modern AI GPU clusters, cloud computing systems, and "time-sensitive systems" like financial trading platforms and massive multi-player games. description: This is an advanced course that will focus on modern machine learning algorithms for autonomous robots as an embodied intelligent agent. description: How can we design AI systems that are not only powerful but also provably safe and trustworthy? This advanced PhD seminar surveys algorithmic methods to enforce hard constraints in machine learning, reinforcement learning, and generative AI. Students will critically assess the strengths and limitations of these methods and develop final projects that apply or extend them in real-world domains. Prerequisites: optimization at the level of CME 307 or EE 364a.
